entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Francesco Orazio della Penna, born Luzio Olivieri, was a Capuchin missionary to Tibet who became prefect of the Tibetan Mission.

Born around 1680, della Penna joined the Capuchin Order at a young age and was ordained as a priest in 1700. He arrived in Tibet in 1716, where he worked tirelessly to spread Christianity and establish a foothold for European influence. Della Penna's tireless efforts paid off in 1732, when the Tibetan government officially recognized the Capuchin Mission as a legitimate presence in the region.

As prefect of the Tibetan Mission, della Penna played a crucial role in shaping the region's religious and cultural landscape. He established a network of monasteries, schools, and hospitals, and worked to promote cross-cultural understanding between Tibetans and Europeans. Della Penna's legacy extends far beyond his own lifetime, however, as his work laid the groundwork for future generations of missionaries and scholars.

The legacy of della Penna can be seen in the many institutions and cultural artifacts he helped establish in Tibet. Today, the Tibetan Mission remains an important part of Tibetan cultural heritage, and della Penna's contributions are still celebrated by historians and scholars around the world.

In a striking testament to the power of human ingenuity and perseverance, della Penna's own life was cut short when he died in 1745, at the age of 65. Despite his untimely passing, however, della Penna's impact on Tibetan history and culture continues to be felt to this day.
